title: Whetstone sweep findings (findings.json)
description: What `wh check --sweep` prints: one finding per flag of every rule below must, or one per batch for a rule with `batch`; a change-mode rule files none (the `--format json` envelope counts its flags in `data.counts`). The same repository state gives byte-identical findings. Runners (Messo inside Virgil, the reusable GitHub Action elsewhere) act on each by class and stay idempotent by fingerprint.

fingerprint.description: The rule, the repository and the subject: the same across runs for the same subject, so a dismissed finding stays quiet until the subject changes. `wh explain <fingerprint>` resolves it.

subjectDigest.description: Changes exactly when the flagged content does.

class.description: How far a runner may go: open a draft pull request, ask a person first, or open a discussion.

title.description: The rule's statement and where it flagged.

responsibility.description: The rule id that raised the finding.

principle.description: The id of the principle the rule serves, when its source names one in the rulebook; `wh explain` gives the statement. A runner quotes it so the why travels with the finding.

unsure.description: Present only where the rule doubts its own flag; a runner parks such a finding until a person raises it.

sites.description: Present only on a batched rule's finding (`batch: by-file` or `by-crate`): every flag the finding stands for, in source order. The fingerprint is then the rule, the repository and the batch (`by-file:<path>` or `by-crate:<directory>`), stable while the batch exists, and `subjectDigest` covers every site's path and flagged content, so it changes when a site is fixed, added or edited.

line.description: The flagged line; absent when the flag is about the whole file.

text.description: The flagged line, trimmed, or the tool's message for a flag on the whole file.

fix.description: The tool's own fix as a unified diff that applies at the repository root with `git apply`. Present only for formatter and lint rules whose tool can rewrite files; the check never applies it.
